## Scatter · the data {.smaller}

### Two-gene co-expression across three tissues

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
`load_coexpression()` returns one row per sample with expression of two genes
across three tissues — Leaf, Root, Seed. We expect `gene_y` to track `gene_x`
roughly linearly (correlation ≈ 0.9).

```python {code-line-numbers="1-3"}
co = load_coexpression()
co.head(3)
# →           sample tissue  gene_x  gene_y
```

## Building a Scatter · Step 1: the canvas {.smaller}

[Scatter · build]{.eyebrow}

### Frame first: axes, labels, scale

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
Decide what the axes mean before drawing anything. Same recipe every time.

```python {code-line-numbers="1-5"}
co = load_coexpression()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 5))
ax.set_xlabel("gene_x expression (TPM)")
ax.set_ylabel("gene_y expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(0, 12); ax.set_ylim(-2, 20)
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 5
co = load_coexpression()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 5))

ax.set_ylabel("gene_y expression (TPM)")

```

<!-- slide 55 -->
## Building a Scatter · Step 2: the points, coloured by tissue {.smaller}

[Scatter · build]{.eyebrow}

### One on-palette scatter call per tissue

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
Use a small dict mapping each tissue to its on-palette colour, then call
`ax.scatter` three times — once per tissue.

```python {code-line-numbers="1-7"}
pal = {"Leaf": GREEN, "Root": BLUE, "Seed": AMBER}
for tissue, c in pal.items():
    g = co[co.tissue == tissue]
    ax.scatter(g.gene_x, g.gene_y,
               color=c, s=55, alpha=0.8,
               edgecolors=CREAM, label=tissue)
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left")
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 5
co = load_coexpression()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 5))
ax.set_xlabel("gene_x expression (TPM)"); ax.set_ylabel("gene_y expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(0, 12); ax.set_ylim(-2, 20)
pal = {"Leaf": GREEN, "Root": BLUE, "Seed": AMBER}
for tissue, c in pal.items():
    g = co[co.tissue == tissue]
    ax.scatter(g.gene_x, g.gene_y, color=c, s=55, alpha=0.8, edgecolors=CREAM, label=tissue)
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left")
ax.set_title("STEP 2: THE POINTS", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=GREEN, pad=10)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 56 -->
## Building a Scatter · Step 3: the fitted line {.smaller}

[Scatter · build]{.eyebrow}

### `np.polyfit` across all samples, plotted in red so it pops

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
A single linear fit across every tissue is the simplest summary. Compute the
slope + intercept, then `ax.plot` the line over the full x-range.

```python {code-line-numbers="1-4"}
m, b = np.polyfit(co.gene_x, co.gene_y, 1)
xs = np.array([co.gene_x.min(), co.gene_x.max()])
ax.plot(xs, m*xs + b, color=RED, lw=2.2,
        zorder=1, label=f"fit: y = {m:.2f}x + {b:.2f}")
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 5
co = load_coexpression()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 5))
ax.set_xlabel("gene_x expression (TPM)"); ax.set_ylabel("gene_y expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(0, 12); ax.set_ylim(-2, 20)
pal = {"Leaf": GREEN, "Root": BLUE, "Seed": AMBER}
for tissue, c in pal.items():
    g = co[co.tissue == tissue]
    ax.scatter(g.gene_x, g.gene_y, color=c, s=55, alpha=0.8, edgecolors=CREAM, label=tissue, zorder=3)
m, b = np.polyfit(co.gene_x, co.gene_y, 1)
xs = np.array([co.gene_x.min(), co.gene_x.max()])
ax.plot(xs, m*xs + b, color=RED, lw=2.2, zorder=1, label=f"fit: y = {m:.2f}x + {b:.2f}")
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", fontsize=9)
ax.set_title("STEP 3: ADD THE FIT", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=INK, pad=10)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 57 -->
## Building a Scatter · Step 4: the message {.smaller}

[Scatter · build]{.eyebrow}

### Annotate Pearson r, put the finding in the title

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
Compute `r`, drop it onto the plot, and let the title state what we found.

```python {code-line-numbers="1-5"}
r = np.corrcoef(co.gene_x, co.gene_y)[0, 1]
ax.text(0.04, 0.94, f"r = {r:.2f}",
        transform=ax.transAxes,
        fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
ax.set_title("GENE_Y TRACKS GENE_X — STRONG CO-EXPRESSION")
```

The whole recipe: **canvas → points → fit → message.**
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 5
co = load_coexpression()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 5))
ax.set_xlabel("gene_x expression (TPM)"); ax.set_ylabel("gene_y expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(0, 12); ax.set_ylim(-2, 20)
pal = {"Leaf": GREEN, "Root": BLUE, "Seed": AMBER}
for tissue, c in pal.items():
    g = co[co.tissue == tissue]
    ax.scatter(g.gene_x, g.gene_y, color=c, s=55, alpha=0.8, edgecolors=CREAM, label=tissue, zorder=3)
m, b = np.polyfit(co.gene_x, co.gene_y, 1)
xs = np.array([co.gene_x.min(), co.gene_x.max()])
ax.plot(xs, m*xs + b, color=RED, lw=2.2, zorder=1)
r = np.corrcoef(co.gene_x, co.gene_y)[0, 1]
ax.text(0.04, 0.94, f"r = {r:.2f}", transform=ax.transAxes,
        fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", fontsize=9)
ax.set_title("GENE_Y TRACKS GENE_X — STRONG CO-EXPRESSION",
             fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold", color=GREEN, pad=10)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
Scatter recipe: **canvas → points (coloured by category) → linear fit →
annotate r + finding title.**
:::
